knowledge: Patient readings: sex is M (male) or F (female); the birthday is a date value and a later birthday means a younger patient, so the oldest patient has the earliest birthday; a patient's age is the current year minus the birth year, and an underage patient is younger than 18.

Visit readings: an admission of '+' is an in-patient stay and '-' an out-patient visit (a follow-up at the out-patient clinic is '-'); "came to the hospital in <year>" is the year of the visit record, and examination windows are date ranges (e.g. 1994/2/19 is 1994-02-19).
Disease readings: a diagnosis is the disease name (e.g. SLE), and the thrombosis column grades severity -- grade 1 is the most serious, grade 2 a severe degree.

Laboratory readings: each lab figure is its own column (e.g. LDH, UA, PLT, ALB, ANA pattern, anti-cardiolipin); a value is compared against its normal range in the question's own terms (e.g. LDH beyond the normal range is above 500; an abnormal uric acid is at most 8.0 for men; a raised PLT is above 400); an ANA pattern of S is the value 'S'.

Percentages and ratios count the same entities on both sides (patients for a share of patients; visits for a share of visits), times 100 for a percentage, and a ratio divides one such count by another.
